home.steps.01.title: Read a real paper
home.steps.01.body: Each topic is anchored to a focal academic paper and a counter-reading that challenges it. Open-access papers are readable inline.
home.steps.02.title: Engage with the discussion
home.steps.02.body: Write your analysis, build on others' arguments, and react to ideas. Contributions are tagged by stance so you can see the landscape of thought.
home.steps.03.title: Pass the quiz
home.steps.03.body: A short comprehension quiz checks you engaged with the material. Unlimited attempts — it's not a test, it's a gate.
home.steps.04.title: Ask the AI (Pro)
home.steps.04.body: Claude, grounded exclusively in the topic's papers, helps you sharpen your arguments and explore implications — never lectures, always Socratic.
home.hero.title: Think more clearly about technology ethics.
home.hero.subtitle: A learning platform for STEM professionals. Engage with academic papers, structured peer discussion, and an AI grounded in the source material.
home.howItWorks.heading: How it works
home.stem.heading: Built for engineers, scientists, and builders
home.stem.body: Technology ethics is taught as a humanities course. Hard Problem treats it as a domain problem — rigorous, source-grounded, and collaborative. No lectures. No vague frameworks. Just the hard questions.
about.title: About Hard Problem
about.body.p1: Hard Problem is an open-source learning platform where STEM professionals develop philosophical thinking skills through structured engagement with real academic papers on technology ethics.
about.body.p2: It is not a philosophy course delivered to STEM people. It is a STEM-native experience — using humanities tools, grounded in authoritative sources, and structured around peer collaboration.
about.body.p3: Each topic unit centers on a focal paper, a counter-reading that disagrees, a real-world anchor, and a structured discussion space. An AI Reasoning Partner (for subscribers) is grounded in the source material and helps you refine your own arguments rather than doing your thinking for you.
about.body.p4: Built by {camus}. Open source under the MIT license.
